title: Wren and the Promise
premise: Mara Amberdale, a wedding planner who quietly stopped believing in love after the fire that took his family's bakery and his brother, has spent three years living small and safe. When an eleven-year-old letter surfaces—his brother's final words, delayed by a postal error—he learns the fire was no accident and that someone in town has been paying to keep the truth buried. As his bakery lease expires, Mara teams up with Odile, a sharp-tongued insurance investigator with her own guilt, to expose the arson, discovering along the way that belonging is something you claim, not something you're granted. The novel ends with the arsonist's confession forcing a town reckoning, Mara choosing to renew the lease and reopen the bakery under his brother's name, and a tentative, hard-won love with Odile built not on promises but on proof.
about_author: Yara Okonkwo is a former small-town journalist who spent a decade covering courtrooms before turning to fiction about justice that arrives too late and love that arrives anyway. She writes from a converted bakery, a detail she insists is not a coincidence.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We meet Mara orchestrating a stranger's flawless wedding while refusing to attend the reception, then returning to his failing bakery-turned-planning-office. Emotional beat: the hollow competence of a man performing joy he no longer feels, with the lease notice tucked in his drawer like a countdown.

chapters.title: The Undelivered Decade
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A retired postal worker, clearing out dead-mail storage, delivers a water-stained letter postmarked eleven years ago—addressed to Mara in his brother Theo's handwriting. He can't bring himself to open it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as procrastination; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Theo's Last Words
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, flashback threads. Mara finally reads the letter: Theo suspected the bakery's landlord, Aldous Vetch, was planning to burn it for insurance, and begged Mara to leave town before it happened. Emotional beat: guilt reframed—Mara survived not by luck but by a warning he never received in time.

chapters.title: The Investigator at Table Six
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile Ferreira, an insurance investigator, attends the same wedding professionally and clocks Mara's reaction when Vetch's name comes up in a toast. She's been quietly re-examining the Amberdale fire file for years, haunted by her own early sign-off on the claim. Emotional beat: predator and prey ambiguity—she approaches him, and neither knows yet who is hunting whom.

chapters.title: Thirty Days on the Lease
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vetch offers to buy Mara's lease cheap, a suspiciously generous lifeline. Mara, needing money, almost signs—until he notices the offer's fine print waives all claims related to 'prior incidents.' Emotional beat: the seduction of easy escape and the first taste of anger instead of grief.

chapters.title: Cold Files and Warm Bread
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile confronts Mara with the discrepancies in the fire report: accelerant traces never followed up, a fire marshal who retired to a house Vetch's company sold him. They form an uneasy pact. Emotional beat: two guarded people discovering the other's guilt mirrors their own.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mara and Odile interview old neighbors, uncovering that several witnesses recanted statements years ago—and one, Mrs. Okoye, now has a paid-off mortgage she can't explain. Emotional beat: the chilling realization that silence in this town was purchased, and everyone took the money but him.

chapters.title: The Mirror in the Ashes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds Theo's hidden ledger in the bakery's old cellar, showing Theo had documented Vetch's debt and threats—and that Theo confronted Vetch the week before the fire. Emotional beat: devastating self-indictment; Mara realizes he'd blamed himself for surviving when Theo's real fear was for him.

chapters.title: Odile's Signature
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback: years ago, Odile, then a junior adjuster, was pressured to approve Vetch's claim and did, launching her career on a lie. She confesses this to Mara. Emotional beat: the fragile pact nearly shatters—Mara sees in her the machinery that buried his brother.

chapters.title: A Wedding Worth Planning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A couple asks Mara to plan a tiny, imperfect, honest wedding—no spectacle—and working on it, he feels something crack open. He and Odile share a late-night planning session that turns into the first honest conversation either has had in years. Emotional beat: warmth as risk; belief returning against his will.

chapters.title: The Retired Fire Marshal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They track down Marshal Denny Cray, who is dying and terrified. He admits Vetch's people paid him to bury the accelerant report, and he kept a copy as insurance. Emotional beat: the horror of complicity, and the first hard evidence—but Cray won't go public while he's still afraid.

chapters.title: Lease Expiration
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The lease deadline hits; Vetch's lawyer delivers an eviction notice with a smile. Mara, drained and doubting, nearly accepts the buyout again to fund Odile's investigation costs. Emotional beat: rock bottom—the price of survival made literal in a signature line.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okoye's Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mrs. Okoye, moved by Theo's letter, admits Vetch's man paid her to say she saw no one near the bakery that night—but she did see someone: Vetch's nephew, Dorian. Emotional beat: the town's bought silence beginning to break, witness by witness.

chapters.title: Dorian Vetch
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They confront Dorian, now a hollowed-out man drinking away his uncle's money. He hints he was there that night but claims he was sent only to 'scare' Theo, and that someone else lit the match. Emotional beat: the case grows darker—Vetch may have had a second hand in the fire.

chapters.title: The Letter Mara Never Sent
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sorting Theo's things, Mara finds his own unsent reply to Theo's letter, written in the weeks after the fire, full of rage at his brother for 'leaving him behind.' Emotional beat: forgiveness of the dead as rehearsal for forgiving himself; the person in the mirror.

chapters.title: Cray's Last Statement
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Dying Cray agrees to record a full statement, but before Odile can secure it, his house is broken into and the evidence copy stolen. Emotional beat: the enemy is watching; the stakes turn from reputation to safety, and Odile realizes she's burned her own bridges at the insurance company.

chapters.title: The Match
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dorian, terrified after Vetch cuts him off, comes to the bakery at midnight: Vetch lit the fire himself; Dorian held the back door. He'll testify—if Mara protects him. Emotional beat: the moral cost of justice—Mara must shield the man who watched his brother die.

chapters.title: What Vetch Offers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vetch makes Mara a final offer: full ownership of the bakery building, free and clear, in exchange for the ledger and silence. Mara, holding everything he's ever wanted, sees the trap for what it is. Emotional beat: the climax of temptation—survival versus truth, priced exactly.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax. Mara and Odile bring the ledger, Odile's reopened file, Dorian's testimony, and Cray's recorded statement—smuggled out before the break-in—to the county prosecutor. Vetch's lawyer fights dirty, exposing Odile's old claim approval. Emotional beat: everything on the line; the past weaponized against the two people seeking to correct it.

chapters.title: Confession in the Courtroom
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. Vetch, cornered by the ledger's dates and Dorian's testimony, breaks and confesses on the record. Mara, called to testify, speaks Theo's name aloud for the first time in eleven years. Emotional beat: catharsis—justice outside the law's timetable finally arriving inside it; Mara's voice steady.

chapters.title: Reopening Day
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With Vetch's assets frozen, Mara uses settlement funds to buy the building and reopens the bakery under its original name, Theo's handwriting repainted on the sign. The honest little wedding couple holds their reception in the reopened shop. Emotional beat: belonging claimed, not granted; grief and joy sharing a counter.

chapters.title: The Promise, Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. Months later, Mara and Odile stand in the bakery at closing time, no grand declarations—just a shared key, a standing Saturday, and a promise made in the present tense. Mara forgives the man in the mirror. Emotional beat: quiet, earned love; survival transformed into a life worth the price.
